note: ONE shared expectation for two resolvers that cannot call each other. The macOS shell (Sources/HasnaConversationsCore) decides which store the bundled server will use and then builds the environment it hands that server; src/lib/store/index.ts is what the server actually resolves with. They diverged: the shell read 3 env vars, the resolver honours more, and uncovered ones select the local store — so the shell logged store=hosted while the child served local SQLite, silently. Deployment modes no longer exist (owner directive 2026-07-29; knowledge k_ms5wv466_u0jidq): client transport is the API url + key pair alone, and any retired storage-mode variable is a fail-loud error naming the variable. Each arm below carries the input, what the shell must announce, and the exact store-selecting keys the child must receive. Tests/HasnaConversationsCoreTests asserts the shell half; src/lib/store/store-resolution-matrix.test.ts asserts the TypeScript resolver reaches the same store from that child environment. Neither half can drift without the other's test failing.

arms.name: arm1-prefixed-url-and-key
arms.note: The fleet flip signal. Correct before and after the fix.

arms.name: arm2-inherited-prefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: The DB path is the resolver's highest-precedence signal among valid selectors — the shell announces local and the child gets local. The child env carries the DB path and NO retired mode key (a mode key in the child would trip the fail-loud ratchet).

arms.name: arm3-inherited-unprefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: Same as arm2 through the unprefixed alias, which the old shell could not see at all.

arms.name: arm4-inherited-unprefixed-mode-local
arms.note: CONVERSATIONS_MODE is a RETIRED selector: set means refuse, naming the variable. The old resolver treated it as an explicit local pin.

arms.name: arm5-inherited-prefixed-alias-mode-local
arms.note: HASNA_CONVERSATIONS_MODE, the near-miss alias of the one key the old shell did read. Retired: refuse naming the variable.

arms.name: arm19-inherited-unprefixed-storage-mode-local
arms.note: CONVERSATIONS_STORAGE_MODE is retired: set means refuse, naming the variable. This arm proves the announcement names THIS key.

arms.name: arm6-unprefixed-url-and-key-only
arms.note: The mirror-image failure: the old shell saw neither key and refused to start on a configuration the resolver accepts. Failing closed, so an availability bug rather than a correctness one — now resolved and re-emitted under the canonical names.

arms.name: arm2f-fleet-config-beats-inherited-prefixed-db-path
arms.note: THE DEPLOYED SHAPE, and the one the owner is waiting on. The fleet config file names the hosted service; a stray inherited DB_PATH must not silently redirect the app to a different dataset. The file outranks the inherited environment and the DB_PATH never reaches the child.

arms.name: arm4f-fleet-config-beats-inherited-unprefixed-mode-local
arms.note: The fleet config file names the hosted service; a stale inherited mode variable is stripped and cannot steer the store. The child env carries NO mode key.

arms.name: file-fleet-config-names-cloud
arms.note: The fleet config file alone, with nothing inherited, resolves to the hosted service.

arms.name: file-db-path-names-local
arms.note: A config file naming a local DB path resolves to local, announced by that key.

arms.name: env-db-path-only-names-local
arms.note: An inherited DB path alone resolves to local, announced by that key.

arms.name: env-unprefixed-db-path-only-names-local
arms.note: The unprefixed DB path alias is honoured and named as the selector.

arms.name: file-pair-beats-inherited-key-only
arms.note: The file outranks the inherited environment: a stray inherited key cannot turn the file's cloud config into a refusal.

arms.name: file-pair-beats-inherited-url-only
arms.note: The file outranks the inherited environment: a stray inherited URL cannot turn the file's cloud config into a refusal.

arms.name: file-explicit-local-is-honoured
arms.note: A config file carrying a RETIRED storage-mode variable refuses, naming the variable — local is selected by a DB path or by absence of an API pair, never by a mode token.

arms.name: file-deprecated-alias-self-hosted-is-refused
arms.note: self_hosted was a deprecated mode alias; with modes gone it is dead vocabulary and the variable refuses, naming the variable.

arms.name: blank-storage-mode-refuses
arms.note: The ratchet fires on SET, not on non-blank: a blank leftover storage-mode variable is still a stale fragment and names itself.

arms.name: file-url-without-key-refuses
arms.note: Half an API configuration is an error, never a fall-back to local. The reviewer listed this branch as having no evidence behind it.

arms.name: key-without-url-refuses
arms.note: The mirror half: a key with no URL is an error naming the missing URL variable. The old default-host behaviour (mode=cloud + key) is gone with the modes.

arms.name: explicit-cloud-mode-refuses
arms.note: A retired mode variable refuses before any key check: the message names the mode variable itself.

arms.name: unrecognised-mode-refuses
arms.note: The resolver's ratchet rejects every retired mode variable by name; there is no token parsing left to disagree about.

arms.name: non-http-url-refuses
arms.note: assertUsableApiUrl refuses a URL the transport could not use. Mirrored here so the shell does not start a server that will throw.

arms.name: nothing-configured-fails-closed
arms.note: The one deliberate divergence from the TypeScript resolver, and the reason this app exists: with nothing configured the library documents local SQLite as the single-operator default, while the app refuses to start. No child is launched, so the two cannot disagree about a running server.
arms.reasonContains: is missing, so there is no hosted-service configuration to read
